status_meanings.answered: The inspected implementation establishes the answer, including explicit limitations.
status_meanings.open: A qualification or design decision remains unresolved; a discriminating check is supplied.
status_meanings.disputed: A documented or intended invariant conflicts with inspected source or a saved probe.

questions.question: Which operations are actually part of CatalogStore, and is deletion one of them?
questions.evidence: CatalogStore at lines 28-50 exposes get, query, stream, put, export, import_bundle, health and close. No delete method exists.

questions.question: Does a generic put preserve all earlier versions of the same record?
questions.evidence: _write_values at lines 182-191 overwrites the row keyed by record_id. History requires a separate owning service.

questions.question: Does SQLite make absence and version preconditions atomic with the write?
questions.evidence: put at lines 151-180 checks within BEGIN IMMEDIATE and commits or rolls back. The in-memory SQLite absence probe succeeds.

questions.question: Can the in-memory adapter perform the same create-if-absent write as SQLite?
questions.evidence: put at lines 60-65 understands only record_version comparison. absent_create_memory reports StoreError while absent_create_sqlite reports accepted.

questions.question: Are DuckDB version reads and conditional writes one atomic transaction?
questions.evidence: put at lines 111-132 calls get and then INSERT OR REPLACE without an enclosing conditional transaction. This was inspected, not race-tested.
questions.discriminating_check: Run two connections against one disposable database, both updating the same expected version; exactly one must succeed.

questions.question: Does a failed bundle import leave the catalog unchanged on every writable adapter?
questions.evidence: DuckDB import_bundle at lines 139-145 and EphemeralRecordStore import_bundle iterate individual puts; SQLite validates then imports inside one transaction.
questions.discriminating_check: Import a valid record followed by an invalid record and compare the complete pre/post store.

questions.question: Is an unsupported export selection refused consistently across adapters?
questions.evidence: SQLite export at lines 202-207 refuses nonempty selection. In-memory, package JSONL, DuckDB and composite exports ignore their selection argument.

questions.question: Can the string false grant an operation through require_operation?
questions.evidence: supports at lines 49-50 uses bool(value). capability_gate_disagreement confirms require_operation permits write='false' while negotiate refuses it.

questions.question: Do unknown or unresolved compatibility declarations permit catalog reads?
questions.evidence: negotiate at lines 71-76 returns a nonpermitting verdict; permits at lines 44-54 refuses unresolved outcomes.

questions.question: Does the composite reject different bodies for an encountered identical identifier and version?
questions.evidence: get at lines 71-88 and _merged_records at lines 93-109 compare complete finite-JSON signatures and refuse conflicts.

questions.question: Which version is returned when different stores hold different versions and no version is requested?
questions.evidence: get keeps the first encountered record at lines 86-87. It does not select the greatest semantic version.

questions.question: Does a paginated composite query establish that all source stores are conflict-free?
questions.evidence: _merged_records explicitly limits its claim to encountered rows; iter_query_records can end before later conflicting stores are visited.

questions.question: Are pages stable while records change or adapters return different native row order?
questions.evidence: SQLite streams SELECT without ORDER BY at line 144; the shared query contract has offset but no ordering or snapshot token.
questions.discriminating_check: Repeat successive pages with concurrent insertion and across adapters, checking for duplicate or skipped identifiers.

questions.question: Can two callers both create a versioned record with expected_version=None?
questions.evidence: revise at lines 113-125 separates the absence read and unconditional put. concurrent_revise_create returned accepted for both synchronized callers.

questions.question: Are the history row and current-version update committed together?
questions.evidence: revise writes _revision_record at line 123 before the guarded current put at line 127. No multi-record transaction surrounds them.
questions.discriminating_check: Inject failure after history insertion and before current update; inspect whether incomplete revisions are reported explicitly.

questions.question: Does reading an old version preserve caller attributes beginning revision_?
questions.evidence: version_record removes all such keys at lines 158-159. revision_attribute_preservation loses revision_customer_field and changes its digest.

questions.question: Does history recompute preserved-record digests before reporting them?
questions.evidence: history reads attributes.revision_digest directly at lines 138-139; version_record reconstructs content without comparing that digest.
questions.discriminating_check: Tamper only a preserved payload and require history, diff and rollback to reject it.

questions.question: Are a caller's mutable query attributes detached before backend iteration?
questions.evidence: IntelligenceQuery copies attributes and snapshot_query reconstructs the typed request; iter_query_records binds the snapshot at call time.

questions.question: Does an empty IntelligenceQuery itself restrict tenant, namespace or lifecycle?
questions.evidence: All facet sequences default empty and matching treats them as unrestricted. Caller-owned authorization must add scope.

questions.question: Which installed server-database adapter provides a durable multitenant deployment?
questions.evidence: Inspected adapters cover in-memory, package JSONL, SQLite, DuckDB and DuckDB over local files. The storage decision names a server database as future work.
questions.discriminating_check: Demonstrate a registered remote adapter with authenticated namespace enforcement, concurrent writes, recovery and a versioned handshake.

questions.question: What are the exact four persistent layer names?
questions.evidence: LAYERS at lines 56-57 names context_intelligence, code_intelligence, runtime_history_solution_intelligence and user_feedback_intelligence.

questions.question: Does build_intelligence_catalog read all four layers through CatalogStore?
questions.evidence: Lines 291-367 use Context registry projections, source-module cards, RunHistory.load and AdviceStore. The result is a dictionary of lists of StoreRecord.

questions.question: Do the documented materialize_intelligence_ref and positional query examples match current entry points?
questions.evidence: The current implementation requires IntelligenceSearchRequest and exposes load_intelligence_item. INTELLIGENCE-AS-LOOPS.md still uses older positional calls and output keys.
questions.discriminating_check: Execute each documentation snippet against the installed package with no model calls.

questions.question: Does the history search card preserve unknown provider token usage as unknown?
questions.evidence: Lines 343-346 sum prompt_tokens and eval_tokens through get(...,0) and or 0, collapsing missing values to zero.

questions.question: Are corrupt or unreadable saved runs counted in catalog results?
questions.evidence: Lines 332-337 silently continue after selected load errors. No excluded-run list is returned by this builder.

questions.question: Does the default four-layer builder use SolveRequest.runs_dir?
questions.evidence: solve_dependencies installs solve_intelligence_catalog(), which returns the bare build_intelligence_catalog function. _installed_catalog invokes it with no arguments.
questions.discriminating_check: Supply separate default and request run roots and inspect the selected history identifiers without exposing real user data.

questions.question: Does four-layer search restrict advice by the requesting user, run, or target?
questions.evidence: advice_records_for_search at lines 324-346 returns every nonretired advice row. The default four-layer request supplies no target/actor filter.
questions.discriminating_check: Place two synthetic users' scoped guidance in one host collection and require authorized search to omit the other user's title and body.

questions.question: Are explicit inactive lifecycle records excluded from normal retrieval?
questions.evidence: query_intelligence at lines 486-499 rejects draft, generated, staged, candidate, validated, deprecated, quarantined, rejected, superseded and retired states unless review is requested.

questions.question: Does include_candidates also admit records in the gated tier?
questions.evidence: The gated-tier branch at lines 496-497 excludes those records independently of include_candidates.

questions.question: Does top_n bound the final unified query result count?
questions.evidence: Lines 515-522 multiply by the number of populated layers and no final trim follows. query_top_n requested one and returned four.

questions.question: Are complete histories loaded only after a search result is selected?
questions.evidence: build_intelligence_catalog at lines 324-359 loads and projects every eligible run before query ranking. Selected materialization later returns the small card.

questions.question: Does a built-in module search card establish an invokable qualified capability?
questions.evidence: Lines 295-319 explicitly create module_reference records with implemented maturity. They do not bind a qualified entrypoint.

questions.question: Are saved SolutionLibrary assets added by the default four-layer builder?
questions.evidence: SolutionLibrary has its own supplied SolverStore-compatible interface; build_intelligence_catalog does not consume it. The component README explicitly records this limit.

questions.question: Does orientation retain the full selected intelligence reference and exact version?
questions.evidence: _four_layer_search at lines 149-159 projects scalar fields and drops intelligence_item_ref. Version and payload_digest are read from absent top-level hit fields rather than the nested reference.

questions.question: Are duplicate Context record identifiers checked for conflicting content?
questions.evidence: The local add helper at lines 28-31 keeps the first record by identifier and silently ignores later duplicates without content comparison.

questions.question: Are the lexical and hash-vector indexes built anew for each four-layer query?
questions.evidence: query_intelligence creates a new Retriever. Retriever.__init__ at lines 354-388 builds both selected backends even for lexical-only searches.

questions.question: Can external retrieval engines register through backend_handshakes?
questions.evidence: backend_handshakes returns descriptive records. Constructor branches at lines 361-387 accept fixed backend names; there is no dynamic registration hook here.

questions.question: Can an index failure be distinguished from a legitimate empty search?
questions.evidence: SqliteFtsBackend.search and LanceDbBackend.search catch any exception and return an empty list at lines 250-251 and 282-283.

questions.question: Can an eligible record disappear because filtering occurs after a bounded ranking pool?
questions.evidence: Backend pools are limited at lines 404-407 before facet_match. postfilter_candidate_starvation returned no hits although allowed matched the query.

questions.question: Does the prefer score affect ordering before the final result limit?
questions.evidence: Fused results are sorted at line 420; preference is calculated at lines 423-432 and no resort follows before the break.
questions.discriminating_check: Use two equal lexical candidates whose preference should reverse the initial order and assert the preferred candidate is selected.

questions.question: Does bodies_never_in_index accurately describe the searchable text placed in indexes?
questions.evidence: backend_handshakes declares it true, but record_search_text includes text and template fields and feeds the combined text into SQLite and LanceDB indexes.

questions.question: Can selecting model2vec cause a model download without a typed network decision?
questions.evidence: Model2VecBackend.__init__ calls StaticModel.from_pretrained at line 311. No effect authority appears in its constructor; no download was run during this audit.
questions.discriminating_check: Start with an empty cache under denied network authority and require refusal before any request.

questions.question: Does model2vec record the actual downloaded model revision and measured dimensions?
questions.evidence: Its EmbeddingSpace is constructed with revision='hf-cache-pin' and dims=256 at lines 324-325, regardless of the supplied model identifier.

questions.question: Who removes LanceDB temporary indexes and closes retrieval connections?
questions.evidence: LanceDbBackend uses tempfile.mkdtemp at line 271 and no close method is present in the inspected backend or Retriever definitions.
questions.discriminating_check: Repeatedly construct and dispose a retriever, measuring temporary directories and open descriptors.

questions.question: Does the hash backend distinguish lexical morphology from learned semantic retrieval?
questions.evidence: hash_vector at lines 145-157 implements token and character features. The capability note explicitly disclaims semantic synonym matching.

questions.question: Does an ordinary inline Context reference bind the selected body text?
questions.evidence: intelligence_package_from_record leaves payload_digest empty without a supplied body digest. inline_digest_binding loaded changed text using the same reference.

questions.question: Who computes the digest of an externally materialized body?
questions.evidence: load_intelligence_ref at lines 346-359 compares MaterializedPayload.digest with the reference. Computing that observed digest is the supplied resolver's responsibility.

questions.question: Does the reference envelope digest bind effects, contracts, modes and maturity?
questions.evidence: IntelligenceItemPackage.digest at lines 170-174 includes item_id, layer, payload_ref, payload_digest and version only.

questions.question: Does projecting StoreRecord into a reference preserve body.version?
questions.evidence: intelligence_package_from_record at lines 249-260 constructs IntelligenceItemHandshake without a version argument, so it uses 1.0.0.

questions.question: Can a candidate Code reference execute through the direct helper without admission?
questions.evidence: execute_code_ref at lines 581-607 has no lifecycle/admission authority argument. candidate_direct_execution returned 7 with lifecycle=candidate and an empty admission_ref.

questions.question: Does execute_code_ref prove that the requested entrypoint is one of the qualified entrypoints?
questions.evidence: The request carries a string entrypoint and resolver/binder; the direct helper does not load CodeAssetSpec or compare its entrypoints.
questions.discriminating_check: Ask for a different callable in a materialized mapping and require exact admission refusal before binding.

questions.question: Does a cached external handle get revalidated before later use?
questions.evidence: MaterializationCache at lines 547-559 returns the cached object by digest or locator without rehashing the current body.
questions.discriminating_check: Change a backing file after first resolution and require the next invocation to detect the changed bytes.

questions.question: Are package installation and repository checkout implemented by the Code template records themselves?
questions.evidence: The strings are load_strategy values. execute_code_ref delegates loading to a supplied resolver and binder; no automatic installer or checkout implementation appears on this path.

questions.question: Does changing a Code asset's dataset references invalidate its qualification digest?
questions.evidence: qualification_digest omits data_refs. The probe changes data_refs, changes card_digest, and keeps qualification_digest unchanged.

questions.question: Does CapabilityAuthority recheck current registered state and exact admission before returning an active asset?
questions.evidence: active_spec at lines 334-351 requires registered state and rebinds the stored admission to the exact asset digest set.

questions.question: Does Code asset admission reject the same producer and verifier identity?
questions.evidence: CodeAssetAdmissionRecord compares casefolded identities at lines 355-357. The authenticated meaning of those identities remains a host responsibility.

questions.question: Can the capability producer promote its own validated asset through CapabilityAuthority?
questions.evidence: promote_as_loop compares promoter_id with producer at lines 556-559 and refuses equality.

questions.question: Are qualification records, transitions and the lifecycle pointer updated atomically?
questions.evidence: qualify_as_loop and promote_as_loop perform several separate puts followed by a guarded state put; CatalogStore provides no common transaction context.
questions.discriminating_check: Inject failures and concurrent transitions after every put; require one committed lifecycle or an explicit recoverable incomplete state.

questions.question: Does _put_immutable prevent conflicting simultaneous first insertion?
questions.evidence: Lines 131-137 check absence and then put without an absence precondition, leaving the same class of creation race reproduced in versioning.
questions.discriminating_check: Synchronize two distinct bodies with one immutable record identifier and require exactly one accepted insertion.

questions.question: Can a stale or forged projection override current capability eligibility?
questions.evidence: _authoritative_match reloads active_spec and compares contract, effect, environment, privacy, tenant and admission fields. invoke_capability_as_loop repeats eligibility before executing.

questions.question: Can an older rebuild replace the active projection pointer after a newer rebuild?
questions.evidence: rebuild_capability_projection_as_loop writes capability_projection_manifest.active unconditionally at line 155.
questions.discriminating_check: Complete rebuilds in reversed version order and require an explicit policy or precondition to prevent accidental rollback.

questions.question: Does task compilation choose a template or infer semantic task type?
questions.evidence: compile_task_value preserves original input, reports advisory template candidates, keeps task_type/output_kind unknown and binding None.

questions.question: Do input/output contracts and maturity participate in TaskTemplate identity?
questions.evidence: content_digest at lines 353-364 omits both contracts and maturity. template_contract_identity demonstrates equal digests and accepted conflicting registration.

questions.question: Can the template library retrieve both old and new versions after registration?
questions.evidence: The dictionary is keyed only by template_id at lines 159-173. A later different version replaces the earlier entry.

questions.question: Does template search exclude deprecated templates from ordinary candidates?
questions.evidence: search at lines 187-199 ranks every stored template without checking maturity. Selection remains advisory.

questions.question: Are captured instructions kept distinct from unexamined external data references?
questions.evidence: TaskIntake.external_source_refs returns empty for FILE_INTAKE; CapturedInstructionProvenance binds text, source bytes and capture method.

questions.question: Does the reference memory store return contradiction groups for conflicting selected claims?
questions.evidence: _detect_conflicts reads result.record, but MemorySearchResult contains only ref/score/refusal fields. memory_conflicts selected two conflicting claims and returned no conflicts.

questions.question: Does max_candidates actually bound records considered by memory ranking?
questions.evidence: MemoryQuery accepts and serializes max_candidates, but rank_records iterates all records and InMemoryMemoryStore.query does not enforce it.

questions.question: Which version does get return when no version is supplied?
questions.evidence: get at lines 37-41 returns the first appended version, not the most recent. CandidateJournal.as_store separately projects latest versions.

questions.question: Does the memory query scope distinguish two projects or two users?
questions.evidence: The query carries a MemoryScope category, not a project/user identity. Separate journal roots or another authorized host boundary must provide identity isolation.

questions.question: Can a client choose another writer identity for a shared-memory request?
questions.evidence: memory_handlers rejects writer_id in payload and passes the authenticated tenant_id to SharedMemory.write at lines 123-133.

questions.question: Does each shared-memory update advance the version used to reject stale writers?
questions.evidence: write accepts any nonempty record_version and does not require advancement. same_version_shared_writes accepted both updates with the same expected version on SQLite.

questions.question: Is RunNoteBoard durable or automatically promoted into persistent intelligence?
questions.evidence: Notes live in an instance list. Reads return detached copies and to_curation_candidates emits candidate records. There is no persistence or automatic promotion here.

questions.question: Are completed journal appends flushed to durable storage?
questions.evidence: CandidateJournal._append at lines 75-78 writes a line, flushes and calls fsync.

questions.question: Can multiple writers safely assign one journal sequence and predecessor chain?
questions.evidence: _next_entry reads the current history before a separate append; no file lock or compare-and-swap surrounds lines 183-203 and 59-78.
questions.discriminating_check: Run two journal instances with synchronized tail reads and require a single ordered, valid chain after both return.

questions.question: Does every CandidateJournal query verify the entire chain before serving active records?
questions.evidence: query delegates to as_store at lines 244-245. as_store checks latest lifecycle/action but does not call validate_journal.

questions.question: Does the public learned-memory projection verify the journal and bound its size?
questions.evidence: learned_memory_for_solve checks a four-megabyte limit and validate_journal before querying, and returns typed unavailable statuses.

questions.question: Do command-line learning and public solve use the same default journal location?
questions.evidence: CandidateJournal defaults to the configured memory root or .loop-engine/memory, while solve reads request.runs_dir/learning and serves nothing if runs_dir is empty.

questions.question: Does AdviceStore recover a truncated final JSON line after interruption?
questions.evidence: _rows at lines 191-194 decodes every nonempty line without recovery. _append has no transaction, fsync or partial-record marker.
questions.discriminating_check: Interrupt a synthetic append and require explicit corruption status without losing prior readable records.

questions.question: Can two AdviceStore instances generate the same identifier in the same millisecond?
questions.evidence: leave_advice combines time in milliseconds with a per-instance counter seeded from the file, without an interprocess reservation.
questions.discriminating_check: Freeze the clock, initialize two writers from the same history, and verify distinct advice identities.

questions.question: Can one Harness Intelligence identity be re-registered with a different body digest?
questions.evidence: HarnessIntelligenceCatalogue.register at lines 161-165 refuses a changed digest for an existing identity.

questions.question: Can the same identity and body digest be re-registered with changed effects or source metadata?
questions.evidence: register compares only held.digest and then replaces the whole item at line 166. It does not compare effects, source_ref, licence or tags.

questions.question: Does a bodies entitlement also verify source qualification and tenant disclosure scope?
questions.evidence: _item checks style, kinds and request-declared effects. _read checks the generic entitlement and body digest. No source admission or tenant-specific record scope is resolved.

questions.question: Can a body read return metered=true when no meter exists?
questions.evidence: The meter callback is optional at lines 200-201; the response unconditionally reports metered=true at line 205.

questions.question: Does ProvisioningServer itself expose an authenticated network protocol endpoint?
questions.evidence: The module explicitly provides no transport. handle accepts local typed requests; the separate ServiceApplication endpoints do not wire this catalogue.

questions.question: Does importing a skill, repository or trace activate it for normal execution?
questions.evidence: HarnessIntelligenceCandidate requires candidate lifecycle, and to_store_record emits experimental tier with executable=false.

questions.question: Are tests checked as typed, unique ExportedFile values just like package source files?
questions.evidence: SolutionExportSpec validates files and their uniqueness at lines 138-147, but merely converts tests to a tuple at line 153.

questions.question: Does changing the container configuration change the export specification digest?
questions.evidence: digest at lines 157-164 omits container settings. export_spec_identity reports equal digests with different rendered Jobs.

questions.question: Does verify_export recompute and verify manifest_digest before returning it?
questions.evidence: Lines 341-380 load the manifest and return its stated digest without recomputation. The mocked probe returns the literal unverified digest.

questions.question: Are manifest file paths revalidated as confined, nonsymlink paths during verification?
questions.evidence: verify_export joins root/path directly at lines 347-354. The mocked tree accepts ../outside.py; no real outside file was accessed.

questions.question: Does a failed integrity or forbidden-content check prevent code execution?
questions.evidence: After recording failed checks, verify_export calls _run_isolated at line 358. The mocked runner was called once after a failing digest check.

questions.question: Is package_name from a loaded manifest validated before interpolation into Python code?
questions.evidence: The loaded package string at line 345 is inserted into source at lines 359 and 375. The safe mock captured the supplied audit_marker statement.

questions.question: Do the isolated Python flags confine file, network and process effects?
questions.evidence: _isolated_python uses -I/-S and _run_isolated uses subprocess.run on the host. No operating-system sandbox or network policy is installed by this code.

questions.question: Can verification pass without running any tests or customer entry point?
questions.evidence: Tests run only if the tests directory exists; entry-point checks run only when run_arguments is supplied. The result accepts all checks that happened to run.

questions.question: Does site_packages verification prove a clean install with declared dependencies only?
questions.evidence: The site_packages mode uses the current interpreter with -I. It does not build a wheel, install into a fresh environment or validate a dependency lock.

questions.question: Are the generated container and scheduling definitions ready to deploy by default?
questions.evidence: ContainerSpec defaults to an unpinned base image. render_kubernetes_job writes IMAGE_REFERENCE. No image build or cluster qualification runs in verify_export.

questions.question: Does the export example establish general fresh-input task correctness?
questions.evidence: The example checks a specific conformance fixture and existence of outputs. It does not independently qualify arbitrary exported solutions or new task populations.

questions.question: Is the passed verification report bound to the exact selected graph before marking it verified?
questions.evidence: solutions_space_from_adaptive uses the last passed report without matching its subject. The probe marks a graph verified with report_digest=unrelated.

questions.question: Does deserialization reject an incorrect solutions-space content digest?
questions.evidence: from_dict at lines 146-150 ignores content_digest. solution_projection_trust confirms acceptance of an incorrect digest.

questions.question: Can adding the same graph with newly verified status update a previously candidate member?
questions.evidence: add_member at lines 119-123 returns the existing space when the graph digest already exists, without updating status or evidence.
